questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 12, and their product is 31,104. How many such pairs of numbers are possible?
questions.questionHtml: The HCF of two numbers is 12, and their product is 31,104. How many such pairs of numbers are possible?
questions.solution:
HCF = 12

Let numbers be:
a = 12x
b = 12y

Given product:
(12x)(12y) = 31104
144xy = 31104
xy = 216

Now,
216 = 2³ × 3³

For HCF(x, y) = 1, whole prime powers must go fully to one side.

Possible coprime pairs:
(1, 216)
(8, 27)

So original number pairs:
(12, 2592)
(96, 324)

questions.question: The sum of the digits of the greatest number that will divide 1359, 1871 and 2767 leaving the same remainder 15 in each case is:
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the digits of the greatest number that will divide 1359, 1871 and 2767 leaving the same remainder 15 in each case is:
questions.solution:
To get the required number:

Since same remainder 15 is left, subtract 15 from each number:

1359 − 15 = 1344
1871 − 15 = 1856
2767 − 15 = 2752

Now find HCF of:

1344, 1856, 2752

HCF = 64

So greatest required number = 64

Sum of digits of 64 = 6 + 4 = 10

questions.question: In a room with dimensions 20m × 15m × 12m has a rectangular window of dimension 1m × 2m through which fresh air flows into the room. What should be the airflow rate (in m/min) through the window per unit area so that one-fourth of the air in the room would change every hour?
questions.questionHtml: In a room with dimensions 20m × 15m × 12m has a rectangular window of dimension 1m × 2m through which fresh air flows into the room. What should be the airflow rate (in m/min) through the window per unit area so that one-fourth of the air in the room would change every hour?
questions.solution:
Room dimensions = 20 m × 15 m × 12 m

Volume of room = 20 × 15 × 12
= 3600 m³

One-fourth air to be changed per hour:
Required volume per hour = 3600/4 = 900 m³

Window area = 1 × 2 = 2 m²

Let airflow rate per unit area = v m/min

Total air entering per minute = 2v m³

In 60 minutes:
Air entered = 2v × 60 = 120v

Given 120v = 900

v = 900/120
v = 7.5 m/min

questions.question: A large cuboid-shaped container has the following dimensions: length = 15 meters, width = 8 meters, and height = 6 meters. A cube-shaped object with an edge length of 4 meters is placed inside the container. How many such cubes can be placed inside the container without any part sticking out?
questions.questionHtml: A large cuboid-shaped container has the following dimensions: length = 15 meters, width = 8 meters, and height = 6 meters. A cube-shaped object with an edge length of 4 meters is placed inside the container. How many such cubes can be placed inside the container without any part sticking out?
questions.solution:
Container dimensions = 15 m × 8 m × 6 m
Cube edge = 4 m

Number of cubes along:

Length = 15 ÷ 4 = 3 cubes
Width = 8 ÷ 4 = 2 cubes
Height = 6 ÷ 4 = 1 cube

Total cubes = 3 × 2 × 1
= 6 cubes
